about: wl-preproc's Engbert-Kliegl saccade detector in true visual angle (design spec 2026-10-30-true-angle-saccades-design.md). Gaze is in degrees per axis; a position (x, y) is the direction normalize(tan x, tan y, 1). velocity_deg_s: for each sample n, samples n-2..n+2 in the local frame at n's direction (azimuthal-equidistant; ex = normalize(x - (x.c)c), ey = c x ex), then (p[n+2] + p[n+1] - p[n-1] - p[n-2]) * fs / 6; the two samples at each edge are 0. eta_deg_s = lambda times each axis's median scale, sqrt(median(v^2) - median(v)^2) or 0, over complete windows only: a sample and the two on each side all available, so neither the edges nor any sample whose window touches a masked one. A sample is in an event when (vx/eta_x)^2 + (vy/eta_y)^2 > 1, runs shorter than min_duration_samples dropped. Size: the angle between the first and last samples' directions, atan2(|u x v|, u.v); a run is a saccade at or above microsaccade_max_deg. Direction: atan2 of the end's local coordinates about the start. Every angle in degrees, polar angles and directions in [0, 360) (mod 360, 0 where that rounds to 360); null for a polar angle at zero eccentricity and a direction with no displacement. Peak speed: the largest |velocity| over the run. A direction is computed here as normalize(sin x cos y, cos x sin y, cos x cos y), the same direction as normalize(tan x, tan y, 1); computed otherwise, or on another C library, the last places differ. Intervals and labels are exact; every other number is held to |got - want| <= 1e-9 + 1e-12 * |want|, in its own unit, since a velocity component near zero is a cancelling difference that loses relative digits. inputs_from names the file a trace's inputs were read from. A run is [start, stop) in samples. Never edited.
